ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Your buddy brags about a 60% win rate.
You lost money last month at 55%.
Something doesn't add up.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors track wins and losses.
They ignore the size of each bet and the odds they took.
That's the trap.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Units fix that.
One unit = a fixed stake, usually 1-2% of your bankroll.
Every bet is measured the same way, regardless of sport or odds.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: You go 6-4 (60%) but bet 1u on winners and 3u on losers.
Net result: -4u. Losing month.
Now flip it: 5-5 (50%) with 2u winners and 0.5u losers. Net: +7.5u. Winning month.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Win rate tells you how often you're right.
Units tell you how much you actually made.
We track both, publicly, every day. 271-229 on the year, +47.0u.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate is the most misleading number in sports betting. Units are what actually matter. 271-229, +47.0u this season.
